instruction: In the git repository at /echo, gather repository-history context about middleware/proxy.go. Run: `cd /echo && git log --oneline -20`, `git log -3 --format='%H %ad %s' --date=iso`, `git log --oneline -10 -- middleware/proxy.go`, `git describe --tags 2>/dev/null; git tag | tail -5`, and `grep -n -i 'proxy' CHANGELOG.md | head -40`. Also run `grep -rn 'ServiceUnavailable' /echo --include=*.go | head -20`. Report all command outputs verbatim. Do NOT edit any file and do NOT fetch anything from the network.

In the Go repository at /echo (labstack/echo v4), run the full test suite and report exactly which tests fail BEFORE any edits. Steps: `cd /echo && go version && go env GOFLAGS && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -60`. Then, for any failing package, run `go test -run <pattern> -v ./middleware/ 2>&1 | tail -80` to get details. Report: (a) the go version, (b) the exact list of failing test names (package::TestName), (c) the failure output snippets. Do NOT edit any file. Just report findings verbatim.

Investigate and fix a bug in /echo/router.go (Go, labstack/echo v4). Only edit /echo/router.go; never modify existing *_test.go files (temporary test files must be deleted before you finish).

GOAL: the hidden test `TestRouterNoRoutablePath` (package echo, not present in the repo) must pass. Its name suggests the router must handle a request path that has no routable match (e.g. a path that cannot match any registered route, an empty path, or a path whose segments are not routable) without panicking and by falling back to the not-found handler.

STEP 1: read /echo/router.go (especially `func (r *Router) Find(method, path string, c Context)`, `Add`, `insert`, `backtrackToNextNodeKind`) and /echo/router_test.go to learn the existing test style. Write a TEMPORARY file /echo/zz_router_tmp_test.go (package echo) with candidate tests TestZZRouterCandA..F reproducing plausible variants:
(A) e:=New(); e.GET("/users/:id", h); Find(GET, "/users", ctx) -> must not panic, handler must be NotFoundHandler.
(B) Find with path "" on a router with routes -> no panic, NotFoundHandler.
(C) Find with a path not starting with "/" (e.g. "foo") -> no panic.
(D) e.GET("/*", h) then Find(GET, "/a/b/c") -> matches.
(E) routes with params+static children, Find a path that backtracks (e.g. routes "/users/new" and "/users/:id") for path "/users/unknown" -> param route matches; and for a path that matches nothing -> NotFoundHandler.
(F) Find with trailing slash variants.
Use `e.NewContext(httptest.NewRequest(http.MethodGet, path, nil), httptest.NewRecorder())` and check `c.Handler()`/`c.Path()`; recover from panics with defer+recover and report the panic message. Run `cd /echo && go test -run 'TestZZRouterCand' -v . 2>&1 | tail -100` and report which candidates FAIL/panic and why.

STEP 2: fix the defect in /echo/router.go with the minimal change that makes the failing behaviour correct (no panic, correct NotFoundHandler fallback) while keeping every existing test in package echo green. Do not change public API, do not touch other files, do not modify existing tests.

VERIFY: `cd /echo && gofmt -l router.go && go build ./... && go vet . && go test -v . 2>&1 | tail -80` (all package echo tests must pass) and `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30`. Then DELETE /echo/zz_router_tmp_test.go and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only router.go modified. Report the diff, before/after candidate results, and full outputs.

Investigate and fix a bug in /echo/group.go (Go, labstack/echo v4). Only edit /echo/group.go; never modify existing *_test.go files (temporary test files must be deleted before you finish).

GOAL: the hidden test `TestMultipleGroupSamePathMiddleware` (in package echo, not present in the repo) must pass. It tests that when multiple Groups are created on the SAME path with different middleware, each group's middleware is applied correctly (and a request that matches no route in a group still reaches the group's middleware / returns 404, without the second group's registration clobbering the first group's routes).

Current code of interest in /echo/group.go:

func (g *Group) Use(middleware ...MiddlewareFunc) {
	g.middleware = append(g.middleware, middleware...)
	if len(g.middleware) == 0 {
		return
	}
	// Allow all requests to reach the group as they might get dropped if router
	// doesn't find a match, making none of the group middleware process.
	g.Any("", NotFoundHandler)
	g.Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)
}

STEP 1 (empirical): create a TEMPORARY file /echo/zz_group_tmp_test.go (package echo) containing several candidate tests named TestZZGroupCandA..E that reproduce plausible variants of the hidden test, e.g.:
(A) e:=New(); g1:=e.Group("/group", m1); g2:=e.Group("/group", m2); g1.GET("/hello",h); g2.GET("/world",h); assert GET /group/hello runs m1 only and GET /group/world runs m2 only.
(B) same prefix, same path registered in both groups; assert the last registered handler+middleware wins and no panic.
(C) g1 registers GET "/*" with h; then g2 := e.Group("/group", m2) is created; assert GET /group/anything still reaches g1's handler (currently the second group's Any("/*", NotFoundHandler) registration overwrites it -> 404).
(D) request to an unmatched path under the group prefix must run the group's middleware and return 404.
(E) nested sub-groups via g1.Group("/sub", m2) with same prefix reuse.
Run `cd /echo && go test -run 'TestZZGroupCand' -v . 2>&1 | tail -80` and report which candidates FAIL and exactly why (status codes, headers, panic).

STEP 2 (fix): based on the failures, fix the bug in /echo/group.go with the MINIMAL change that makes the failing behaviour correct while keeping all existing tests green. The most likely intended fix is to avoid clobbering routes registered by other groups that share the same prefix: in `Use`, do not register the catch-all `Any("", NotFoundHandler)` / `Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)` routes again if the group already has routes for that prefix, or (preferred, matching upstream echo) keep the middleware application but make sure the group's own registered routes keep their own middleware. If you conclude the real defect is that `g.Any("", NotFoundHandler)`/`g.Any("/*", NotFoundHandler)` are re-registered and overwrite a previously registered route for the same method+path in another group, guard the registration so it only happens once per group (e.g. track with a bool field on Group or check the router for an existing route) - but ONLY if that makes the candidate tests pass and breaks nothing.

Do NOT add new public API. Do NOT change other files. Do NOT change existing tests.

VERIFY: `cd /echo && gofmt -l group.go && go build ./... && go vet . && go test -v . 2>&1 | tail -60` (all package echo tests must pass) and `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30`. Then DELETE /echo/zz_group_tmp_test.go and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only group.go modified. Report: the diff, which candidate tests failed before/after, and full test output.

Investigate and fix a bug in /echo/middleware/compress.go (Go, labstack/echo v4). Only edit /echo/middleware/compress.go; never modify existing *_test.go files (temporary test files must be deleted before you finish).

GOAL: the hidden test `middleware::TestGzipEmpty` (not present in the repo) must pass. It checks the Gzip middleware's behaviour for an EMPTY response body: when nothing is written to the response body, the response must NOT carry `Content-Encoding: gzip` (and must not be gzip-encoded), while a non-empty response must still be gzipped.

STEP 1: read /echo/middleware/compress.go carefully and write a TEMPORARY file /echo/middleware/zz_gzip_tmp_test.go (package middleware) with candidate tests TestZZGzipCandA..E:
(A) e:=echo.New(); e.Use(Gzip()); e.GET("/", func(c echo.Context) error { return nil }); request with Accept-Encoding: gzip; assert rec.Code==200, rec.Header().Get(echo.HeaderContentEncoding)=="", rec.Body.Len()==0, and body is NOT gzip.
(B) same but handler returns c.NoContent(http.StatusNoContent) -> assert 204 and no Content-Encoding.
(C) same but handler writes an empty string c.String(http.StatusOK, "") -> assert no Content-Encoding header and empty body.
(D) no route registered (404 path) with Accept-Encoding: gzip -> assert 404 and no Content-Encoding.
(E) handler writes "test" -> assert body is valid gzip and Content-Encoding==gzip.
Run `cd /echo && go test ./middleware/ -run 'TestZZGzipCand' -v 2>&1 | tail -80` and report which candidates FAIL and why (status, headers, raw body bytes).

STEP 2: fix the defect in /echo/middleware/compress.go with a minimal change so the failing candidates pass and all existing middleware tests stay green. Likely area: the deferred cleanup block inside GzipWithConfig (`if res.Size == 0 { ... res.Writer = rw; w.Reset(ioutil.Discard) }`) and/or `gzipResponseWriter.Write`/`WriteHeader`. Note that a `gzip.Writer` writes its gzip header on the first Write even when the payload is empty, so a response whose body is empty can still end up with Content-Encoding: gzip and gzip bytes; make sure the Content-Encoding header is removed and the underlying writer restored whenever the response body ends up empty. Do not change public API, do not touch other files.

VERIFY: `cd /echo && gofmt -l middleware/compress.go && go build ./... && go test ./middleware/ -run 'TestGzip|TestDecompress' -v 2>&1 | tail -60` and `cd /echo && go test ./... 2>&1 | tail -30`. Then DELETE /echo/middleware/zz_gzip_tmp_test.go and confirm `git status --porcelain` shows only middleware/compress.go modified. Report the diff, before/after candidate results, and full outputs.
